# dm

dm is a durable terminal multiplexer in one binary. One process is the server; it owns the panes and their pty state, and it keeps running after you leave. A second mode is the TUI client, which draws the panes and sends actions. A third is the CLI, which sends the same actions to the same server, so a script and a hand on the keyboard drive one surface. Detach and reattach, and the shells keep running.

## Identifiers

A workspace is `s1`, `s2`, and so on. A window is `w1`, `w2`. A pane is its window id plus `p` and a per-window sequence: `w2p3` is the third pane opened in window 2. Ids are readable and constructible, and a counter only moves forward, so a closed id is never reused.

## Commands

A command is the first word after `dm`. With no command, `dm` attaches to a session, creating it if needed.

| Command | Arguments | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dm` | `[-s name]` | attach to a session, creating it if needed | `dm -s work` |
| `dm attach` | `[-s name]` | attach to a session, creating it if needed (alias: a) | `dm attach -s work` |
| `dm new` | `[-s name]` | start a session without attaching | `dm new -s work` |
| `dm ls` | `-` | list sessions with pane counts and project (alias: list-sessions) | `dm ls` |
| `dm kill` | `[-s name]` | stop a session's server (panes survive) | `dm kill -s work` |
| `dm purge` | `[--dry-run]` | remove dead sessions whose panes are gone | `dm purge --dry-run` |
| `dm reset` | `[-s name \| --all] --force` | discard a session and its panes for a full restart | `dm reset -s work --force` |
| `dm exec` | `'<json>' [-s name]` | send an action as JSON | `dm exec '{"action":"split","target":"w1p1","dir":"right"}'` |
| `dm write-to` | `<pane> --msg T` | type text into a pane (--enter to accept) (alias: write) | `dm write-to w1p1 --msg 'ls -la' --enter` |
| `dm split` | `<pane> --dir D` | split a pane: left right up down | `dm split w1p1 --dir right` |
| `dm focus` | `<pane>` | focus a pane | `dm focus w1p2` |
| `dm next-pane` | `-` | focus the next pane | `dm next-pane` |
| `dm prev-pane` | `-` | focus the previous pane | `dm prev-pane` |
| `dm rename-workspace` | `<ws> <name>` | rename a workspace | `dm rename-workspace s1 build` |
| `dm set-project` | `<ws> [name]` | set a workspace's project, or clear it with no name | `dm set-project s1 dm` |
| `dm new-window` | `-` | open a new window | `dm new-window` |
| `dm next-window` | `-` | focus the next window | `dm next-window` |
| `dm prev-window` | `-` | focus the previous window | `dm prev-window` |
| `dm status` | `[pane]` | show OSC 7501 agent status | `dm status w1p1` |
| `dm list` | `-` | print panes as a table, or the raw tree with --json | `dm list` |
| `dm dash` | `[-s name]` | print the palette rows | `dm dash` |
| `dm peek` | `<id> [--lines N]` | print the screen a palette row lands on | `dm peek w1p1 --lines 10` |
| `dm wait` | `<pane> [--timeout D]` | stream a pane's output until a command ends, the next one when nothing runs, then name the exit code | `dm wait w1p1 --timeout 10m` |
| `dm read` | `<pane> [--lines N]` | print a pane's screen | `dm read w1p1 --lines 20` |
| `dm read <pane> --scrollback N` | `-` | print N rows above the screen | `dm read w1p1 --scrollback 200` |
| `dm yank` | `<pane> [--lines N]` | print a pane's output since the last Enter | `dm yank w1p1` |
| `dm msg post` | `--state S [--key K] [--msg T] [--body T \| --body-file P]` | post one entry to the box | `dm msg post --key build --state done --msg 'all green'` |
| `dm msg list` | `[--key K \| --prefix P] [--after SEQ] [--limit N] [--json]` | print the box newest first | `dm msg list --key build --limit 20` |
| `dm msg show` | `--key K [--seq N \| --from PANE]` | print one entry's body, or its summary line | `dm msg show --key build --seq 12` |
| `dm msg wait` | `[--key K \| --prefix P] [--state S] [--after SEQ] [--timeout 5m] [--json]` | block until an entry matches | `dm msg wait --key build --state done --timeout 10m` |
| `dm msg sub` | `[--key K \| --prefix P] [--state S] [--after SEQ] [--json]` | stream entries as they arrive | `dm msg sub --prefix build --json` |
| `dm msg clear` | `[--key K \| --prefix P]` | clear one key, or a prefix branch, or the whole box | `dm msg clear --key build` |
| `dm msg watchers` | `[--json]` | print the live watches | `dm msg watchers` |
| `dm msg schema` | `-` | print the box schema the server serves | `dm msg schema` |
| `dm man` | `[-o path]` | print the man page, or write it to a file | `dm man -o dm.1` |
| `dm llms` | `[-o path]` | print llms.txt, or write it to a file | `dm llms -o llms.txt` |
| `dm html` | `[-o path]` | open this page as HTML in a browser, or write it to a file | `dm html -o dm.html` |

## Actions: `dm exec`

`dm exec` takes one JSON object. The fields are:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | the action name, required |
| `target` | the pane, window or workspace id the action acts on |
| `dir` | split or focus direction: left, right, up or down; swap-panes swaps by direction instead of other |
| `other` | the second pane: resize-split, swap-panes and move-pane |
| `msg` | text to type into a pane |
| `enter` | press enter after msg |
| `name` | a new name for a window, workspace or pane |
| `window` | new-workspace: the window name |
| `index` | select-window: the window number; set-rail: the rail width |
| `id` | request id, echoed in the reply |
| `cwd` | working directory for a new pane, window or workspace |
| `ratio` | split ratio, 0 to 1 |
| `nofocus` | do not move focus to the new pane |
| `layout` | select-layout: even-horizontal, even-vertical, main-horizontal, main-vertical or tiled; next cycles the stored preset forward |
| `on` | synchronize-panes: true or false; absent toggles |
| `float` | float-open and float-close: the client-chosen float id |
| `command` | float-open: the command to run instead of the diff command |
| `label` | float-open: the float title, default the command's first word |
| `argv` | split, new-window and new-workspace: the program and arguments a new pane runs instead of a shell |
| `cols` | terminal columns |
| `rows` | terminal rows |
| `keys` | raw bytes to write to a pane |
| `data` | raw bytes |
| `count` | history rows above the screen |
| `res` | the verb payload for the msg-* actions |

The action field names one of these. Each example is one JSON object, carrying only the fields that action needs.

| Action | Example |
| --- | --- |
| `ping`, `list` | `{"action":"ping"}`, `{"action":"list"}` |
| `read` | `{"action":"read","target":"w1p1"}` |
| `history`, `yank` | `{"action":"history","target":"w1p1","count":200}`, `{"action":"yank","target":"w1p1"}` |
| `replay` | `{"action":"replay","target":"w1p1"}` |
| `status` | `{"action":"status","target":"w1p1"}` |
| `write-to` | `{"action":"write-to","target":"w1p1","msg":"go test ./...","enter":true}` |
| `exec` | `{"action":"exec","target":"w1p1","msg":"go test ./..."}` |
| `keys` | `{"action":"keys","target":"w1p1","keys":"Aw=="}` |
| `split` | `{"action":"split","target":"w1p1","dir":"right","argv":["htop"]}` |
| `zoom-pane` | `{"action":"zoom-pane"}` |
| `set-rail` | `{"action":"set-rail","index":30}` |
| `resize-split` | `{"action":"resize-split","target":"w1p1","other":"w1p2","ratio":0.7}` |
| `focus` | `{"action":"focus","target":"w1p2"}` |
| `focus-dir` | `{"action":"focus-dir","dir":"left"}` |
| `next-pane`, `prev-pane` | `{"action":"next-pane"}`, `{"action":"prev-pane"}` |
| `close-pane` | `{"action":"close-pane","target":"w1p1"}` |
| `close-window`, `close-workspace` | `{"action":"close-window","target":"w1"}`, `{"action":"close-workspace","target":"s1"}` |
| `new-window` | `{"action":"new-window","target":"s1","name":"build"}` |
| `next-window`, `prev-window` | `{"action":"next-window"}`, `{"action":"prev-window"}` |
| `select-window` | `{"action":"select-window","index":2}` |
| `new-workspace` | `{"action":"new-workspace","name":"build"}` |
| `next-workspace`, `prev-workspace` | `{"action":"next-workspace"}`, `{"action":"prev-workspace"}` |
| `list-workspaces`, `list-panes` | `{"action":"list-workspaces"}`, `{"action":"list-panes"}` |
| `pane` | `{"action":"pane","target":"w1p1"}` |
| `toggle-fold` | `{"action":"toggle-fold","target":"w1"}` |
| `set-pane-name` | `{"action":"set-pane-name","target":"w1p1","name":"tests"}` |
| `focus-window`, `focus-workspace` | `{"action":"focus-window","target":"w1"}`, `{"action":"focus-workspace","target":"s1"}` |
| `rename-window`, `rename-workspace`, `set-project` | `{"action":"rename-window","target":"w1","name":"build"}`, `{"action":"rename-workspace","target":"s1","name":"build"}`, `{"action":"set-project","target":"s1","name":"dm"}` |
| `swap-panes`, `move-pane` | `{"action":"swap-panes","target":"w1p1","dir":"left"}`, `{"action":"move-pane","target":"w1p1","other":"w1p2","dir":"right"}` |
| `select-layout` | `{"action":"select-layout","layout":"next"}` |
| `synchronize-panes` | `{"action":"synchronize-panes","on":true}` |
| `float-open` | `{"action":"float-open","float":"f1","target":"w1p1","command":"tig"}` |
| `float-close` | `{"action":"float-close","float":"f1"}` |
| `msg-post` | `{"action":"msg-post","res":{"key":"build","state":"done","msg":"all green"}}` |
| `msg-list` | `{"action":"msg-list","res":{"key":"build","limit":20}}` |
| `msg-clear` | `{"action":"msg-clear","res":{"key":"build"}}` |
| `msg-wait` | `{"action":"msg-wait","res":{"key":"build","state":"done","timeoutMs":60000}}` |
| `msg-sub` | `{"action":"msg-sub","res":{"keyPrefix":"lane/","afterSeq":0}}` |
| `msg-watchers`, `msg-schema` | `{"action":"msg-watchers","res":{}}`, `{"action":"msg-schema","res":{}}` |

## Keys

The prefix key is `ctrl+b` by default. A key label is the key pressed after the prefix. The help overlay prints the label; the action name is the one `dm exec` and the config use.

| Keys | Action | Help label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `|` | `split-right` | split right |
| `-` | `split-down` | split down |
| `< / ^` | `split-left / split-up` | split left / up |
| `[` | `scrollback` | scrollback |
| `y / Y` | `copy-output / copy-screen` | copy output / screen |
| `i` | `copy-pane-id` | copy pane id |
| `h j k l` | `focus-left / focus-down / focus-up / focus-right` | focus pane |
| `n / K` | `next-pane / prev-pane` | next/prev pane |
| `x` | `close-pane` | close pane |
| `X` | `close-window` | close window |
| `z` | `zoom-pane` | zoom pane |
| `c` | `new-window` | new window |
| `w / W` | `next-window / prev-window` | next/prev win |
| `0-9` | `window-1 / window-2 / window-3 / window-4 / window-5 / window-6 / window-7 / window-8 / window-9 / window-10` | select window |
| `o / O` | `swap-next / swap-prev` | swap with next / prev pane |
| `u` | `next-layout` | cycle layout |
| `t` | `new-workspace` | new workspace |
| `)` | `next-workspace` | next workspace |
| `S` | `synchronize-panes` | synchronize panes |
| `s` | `picker` | switch session |
| `p` | `command-palette` | command palette |
| `r` | `rename-workspace` | rename workspace |
| `P` | `set-project` | set project |
| `m` | `message-box` | message box |
| `N` | `notification-centre` | notifications |
| `b` | `toggle-rail` | cycle rail: full, thin, hidden |
| `d / q` | `detach / detach-alt` | detach |
| `ctrl+b` | `send-prefix` | send prefix |
| `ctrl+r` | `reload` | reload config |

## Sidebar

The sidebar is a tree of workspaces, windows and panes. A workspace row is a foldable header. Under an unfolded workspace, each window gets a window row with its fold caret, its rendered window label, branch and dirty counts, and a dim note row when that pane has a commit message. The label falls back to the folder, then the window name, when the template renders empty. The source pane is the focused pane when it carries a branch, else the first pane carrying a branch, else the focused pane, else the window's first pane. The window's pane rows follow when the window is unfolded. A folded workspace hides its windows and panes; a folded window hides only its panes. A left click on a workspace row focuses the first available pane in that workspace. A left click on a workspace caret toggles the workspace fold without changing focus. A left click on a window row focuses the first available pane in that window and makes it the active window. A left click on a window caret toggles the window fold without changing focus. A left click on a pane row focuses that pane. Double-clicking a workspace row opens the workspace rename prompt; double-clicking a window row opens the window rename prompt; double-clicking a pane row opens the pane rename prompt. A right click on any row opens the row menu for that row: rename, close, new, fold and focus, as the row allows. The bottom row of the sidebar is its control: a left click there toggles the rail between full and thin. The `toggle-rail` key cycles full, thin and hidden. A window tab bar sits above the pane area, to the right of the rail. One tab per window in the active workspace. A tab is its label plus one padding cell on each side, clamped to `tab-min-width` and `tab-max-width` from `config.kdl` (defaults 8 and 20 cells); a label wider than the maximum is cut with an ellipsis. The tab label, the window row's leading label and the status bar window chip come from the `window-label` Go template, which defaults to the window name for a named window and the id plus repository folder for an unnamed one. Clicking a tab selects that window; double-clicking opens the window rename prompt.

## Config

`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dm/config.kdl`, or `$HOME/.config/dm/config.kdl` when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset, is a patch over the built-in values: a node the file leaves out keeps its built-in value, and an action left out of a `keymap` block keeps its built-in key. dm writes a default file on first run.

| Node | Value | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prefix` | a quoted key name, one sequence | `"ctrl+b"` | Set the prefix key that opens the main keymap. |
| `default-fold` | "fold" or "unfold" | `"fold"` | Set whether a new window's rail starts folded or unfolded. A reload applies it to windows created after it. |
| `tab-min-width` | an integer of at least 3 cells | `8` | Set the smallest tab width in the window tab bar. |
| `tab-max-width` | an integer of at least 3 cells, not below tab-min-width | `20` | Set the largest tab width before the label is cut. |
| `padding` | an integer from 0 to 4 cells | `0` | Set the blank cells between a pane's border and its content. A reload resizes every pane. |
| `history-lines` | an integer from 100 to 32768 lines | `2000` | Set the scrollback window and the pane ring budget: about 256 bytes per line, capped at 8 MiB. |
| `glyphs` | "auto", "ascii", "unicode" or "nerd" | `"auto"` | Choose the glyph vocabulary the chrome draws with. |
| `window-label` | a quoted Go template | `"{{if .Named}}{{.Name}}{{else}}{{.ID}}{{with base .Root}} {{.}}{{end}}{{end}}"` | Set the template that renders a window label. |
| `dashboard-preview` | an integer from 0 to 100 | `60` | Set the share of the dashboard body the preview band opens at. Zero opens on the table alone; the peek key still shows the band. |
| `palette-rows` | an integer of at least 1 | `10` | Set how many entries the command palette shows before it scrolls. A screen too small for the cap holds fewer. |
| `diff-command` | a quoted shell command | `"git diff"` | Set the command the dashboard diff key runs in a floating pane, or in a split pane with the dashboard's diff-split key. It runs through sh -c in the selected pane folder. |
| `dashboard-layout` | "full" or "float" | `"full"` | Draw the dashboard over the whole screen, or as a palette centred over the panes. |
| `float-shadow` | "off" or "on" | `"off"` | Set the drop shadow the floats paint beside and under their box: the prefix help box, the rename prompt and every floating pane. |
| `theme` | a quoted theme name matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ | none | Select a theme from the themes directory beside config.kdl; no node keeps the built-in theme. |
| `keymap` | a quoted mode name and a { "action" "key" } block | `the built-in table` | Patch one keymap mode; an action the file leaves out keeps its built-in key. |
| `command` | a quoted name matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ and a { run "..." } block | `none` | Define a command a keymap can run: bind "command:<name>" to a key and it runs the run text through sh -c in the window's folder. |

## Keymaps

Each mode is a table of actions. The table lists the built-in binding; `dm exec` and a `keymap` node use the action name.

| `help` | `down` | `j` |
| `help` | `down-arrow` | `down` |
| `help` | `page-up` | `pgup` |
| `help` | `page-down` | `pgdn` |
| `help` | `top` | `g` |
| `help` | `bottom` | `G` |
| `help` | `close` | `q` |
| `help` | `close-esc` | `esc` |
| `help` | `close-question` | `?` |

## Theme

A theme file is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dm/themes/<name>.kdl`, named by the `theme` node; no node keeps the built-in theme. Every block and every key is optional, because the file reads over the built-in theme. A colour is `#rrggbb`; a glyph is one rune one cell wide. The built-in values are:

| Block | Keys and built-in defaults | What it carries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `palette` | `rail-bg` #14131a, `rail-focus-bg` #2c2a38, `rail-hover-bg` #21202d, `rail-text` #e9eaf1, `rail-dim` #8f93a8, `rail-header` #a6a9bd, `rail-window` #9599ae, `rail-diff-add` #78dc82, `rail-diff-del` #ff7d7d, `rail-working` #f5be50, `bar-accent` #7ac0eb | Rail and status bar colours. |
| `accents` | `accent-1` #bb9af7, `accent-2` #6edceb, `accent-3` #f08cd7, `accent-4` #7ea9ff, `accent-5` #f0a05a, `accent-6` #8cd79b | Workspace accent colours, assigned in order. |
| `glyphs` | `grip` •, `divider-row` ━, `divider-col` ┃, `border-top-left` ┌, `border-top-right` ┐, `border-bottom-left` └, `border-bottom-right` ┘, `border-horizontal` ─, `border-vertical` │, `border-tee-left` ├, `border-tee-right` ┤, `fold-open` ▾, `fold-closed` ▸, `active-mark` ▸, `workspace-bar` ▌, `dirty` ●, `shadow` ░ | Box, divider, fold and mark glyphs. |
| `states` | `working.glyph` ●, `working.colour` #f5be50, `idle.glyph` ○, `idle.colour` #78c8e1, `blocked.glyph` ▲, `blocked.colour` #ff6e6e, `done.glyph` ✓, `done.colour` #6ee191, `error.glyph` ✕, `error.colour` #ff82a0, `unknown.glyph` ?, `unknown.colour` #8f93a8, `shell.glyph` ▶, `shell.colour` #8f93a8 | Glyph and colour per pane state: working, idle, blocked, done, error, unknown, shell. |

## Prompt marks

dm copies a command's output with prefix y and dm yank. The Enter dm forwards marks where that output starts; the shell's OSC 133 marks make both edges exact. Without them the copy starts after the echoed command line and ends at the last row with content, so the trailing prompt is copied too. With them the copy is the command's output alone, even when the prompt repaints its line on Enter.
zsh emits the marks with one line in ~/.zshrc, before the prompt theme registers its own precmd hook:

```zsh
precmd() { print -Pn '\e]133;D\e\\\e]133;A\e\\' }; preexec() { print -Pn '\e]133;C\e\\' }
```

dm reads `133;A` (the prompt starts, and the output ends there when no D arrives), `133;C` (the command starts, and the copy starts here) and `133;D` (the command ended, and the copy ends here).
The marks are ordinary output, so they travel over ssh and a nested multiplexer like any other bytes. A shell on a remote host needs the same line in its own start file; a pane running a program instead of a shell has no prompt and no marks. dm reads the marks per pane and needs no configuration of its own.
The marks are defined by the semantic prompts proposal: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/Per_Bothner/specifications/blob/master/proposals/semantic-prompts.md

## Environment

| Variable | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `DM_STATE` | State directory; overrides XDG_STATE_HOME. |
| `XDG_STATE_HOME` | State directory base; dm uses $XDG_STATE_HOME/dm. |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | Config directory base; dm reads $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dm/config.kdl. |
| `HOME` | Home directory base; dm reads $HOME/.config/dm and $HOME/.local/state/dm when the XDG variables are unset. |
| `DM_SESSION` | The session a pane belongs to; dm refuses to attach that session from inside it, and refuses a name with no live session, which would nest a new one in the pane. |
| `DM_PANE` | The pane id a pane's shell runs in. |
| `DM_NERD` | 1 forces Nerd Font glyphs, 0 forces the Unicode fallback. |
| `DM_NOTIFY` | 0 turns desktop notifications off. |
| `DM_STATS` | Non-empty prints two stderr lines when the client exits: "dm: style cache: <hits> hits, <misses> misses, <rate>% hit rate" and "dm: pacing: <frames> frames written, <wakes> wakes, <ms>ms interval". |
| `COLUMNS` | Terminal width when the client cannot ask the terminal. |
| `SHELL` | The shell a new pane runs. |
| `TMUX` | Set inside tmux; dm uses it to pick its terminal behaviour. |

## Files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `$DM_STATE/sessions/<name>/state.json` | Session state: workspaces, windows, panes, layouts and names. |
| `$DM_STATE/sessions/<name>/server.sock` | Unix socket the session server listens on. |
| `$DM_STATE/sessions/<name>/panes/<id>.sock` | Unix socket one pane's mux listens on. |
| `$DM_STATE/sessions/<name>/panes/<id>.log` | Pane output log. |
| `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dm/config.kdl` | Prefix, keymaps, commands, default-fold, tab widths, padding, glyphs, window label and theme name; written on first run. |
| `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dm/themes/<name>.kdl` | Theme palette, accents, glyphs and state styles. |

## Recipes

Attach to a session, creating it if needed:

```sh
dm attach -s work
```

Run a command in a pane:

```sh
dm write-to w1p1 --msg 'go test ./...' --enter
```

Read a pane's screen, or rows above it:

```sh
dm read w1p1 --lines 20
dm read w1p1 --scrollback 200
```

Split a pane:

```sh
dm split w1p1 --dir right
```

Close a window and every pane in it:

```sh
dm exec '{"action":"close-window","target":"w1"}'
```

Post to the box and wait on it:

```sh
dm msg post --key build --state done --msg 'all green'
dm msg wait --key build --state done --timeout 10m
```


## Gotchas

- `dm kill` stops a session's server. The panes keep running; attach again and they are there.
- `dm purge` removes dead sessions whose panes are gone. Add `--dry-run` to see the list first.
- `dm reset` discards a session and its panes for a full restart. It needs `--force`; `--all` resets every session.
- `toggle-fold` takes a workspace id, a window id, or `project:<name>` to fold a whole project group.
- A bare word is a session name: `dm work` attaches to `work`, it does not run a command called `work`.
